items.title: ΗΠΑ: Οι απόφοιτοι του MIT κατασκεύασαν ηλεκτρικό θαλάσσιο ανεμόπτερο 50 ποδιών με εμβέλεια 180 μιλίων και ταχύτητα 180 μίλια/ώρα
items.titleOriginal: US: MIT alumni build 50-foot electric seaglider with 180-mile range and 180-mph speed
items.description: Η Regent Craft δημιούργησε ένα ηλεκτρικό θαλάσσιο ανεμόπτερο που μπορεί να ταξιδέψει γρήγορα. Το όχημα ταξιδεύει αρχικά πάνω σε ένα κύτος και στη συνέχεια μεταβαίνει σε υδροπτέρυγα. Στη συνέχεια μπορεί να πετάξει ελαφρώς πάνω από το νερό. Είναι κατάλληλο για μεταφορά εμπορευμάτων και ανθρώπων κατά μήκος των ακτών. Ο Billy Thalheimer και ο Mike Klinker είναι συνιδρυτές του Regent. Το θαλάσσιο πλαγιό τους μήκους 50 ποδιών μπορεί να γ…
items.descriptionOriginal: Regent Craft has created an electric seaglider which can travel quickly. The vehicle initially travels upon a hull and then transitions to hydrofoils. It can then fly slightly above the water. It is suitable for transporting goods and people along coastlines. Billy Thalheimer and Mike Klinker are co-founders of Regent. Their 50-foot seaglider can go as fast as 180 mph and can be driven for up to 180 miles on one charge. Increased efficiency and decreased resistance are provided via ‘ground effect’ where an aircraft benefits from flying near to a surface. Regent’s passenger seaglider (Viceroy) has a wingspan of 65 feet. It can transport up to 14 people, or around 3,500 lb of freight. Potential routes include New York to the Hamptons, Miami to West Palm Beach and inter island travel in Hawaii and Japan. Thalheimer describes it as “a low cost, dependable and quick way to transport people along coastal regions”. Regent develops autonomous seaglider for military missions Regent has also produced a defense focused, more compact seaglider called Squire. It is able to either fly remotely or unattended and can transport objects of up to 50 lb. It can also drive at 80 mph and last 100 nautical miles on a single charge. Regent has conducted test flights with the U.S. Marine Corps for mock supply and rescue operations. Within defense, the seaglider could be used to transport essential supplies such as blood and medical tools to distant regions. In 2022, Squire successfully undertook its initial test flight. Viceroy had its initial flight in September 2026. Both seagliders function in a similar manner. They begin by travelling on a hull. Hydrofoils are then utilized so that the vehicle can speed up. It then ascends slightly and begins to fly. Again, ground effect aids flight and lessens resistance. Thalheimer states that the seaglider is “six times faster than a ferry but will be half the cost of an airline ticket.” Regent moves from early experiments to manufacturing Thalheimer explains that the duo’s passion for ground effect travel was ignited in 2016 when a man-powered plane they were piloting failed during a Red Bull Flugtag event along the Charles River in Boston. They learnt valuable information regarding both engineering and risk assessment. Following MIT, the pair moved to Aurora Flight Sciences a company set up by another MIT alumnus, John Langford ’79, SM ’83, SM ’85, PhD ’87. Here, Thalheimer was involved in developing an eVTOL (electrically powered, vertical take-off and landing) aircraft. However, he realized that extra power sources, ascent and headwinds could all limit the distance it could be driven on a single charge to approximately 50 miles. The founders then investigated using electricity to power a water-based vehicle. As there are no runways in these environments, they concentrated on employing ground effect to further boost driving distance. Furthermore, Regent highlights that electric power not only allows for a less noisy vehicle but also has a lesser environmental effect. The seaglider’s battery and electric motor both contain only one moving component. Prior to entering Y Combinator in 2021, Regent obtained financial support from the E14 venture fund, which is affiliated with MIT. The company has since established a 255,000 square foot production site in North Kingstown, Rhode Island. This is planned to manufacture around 70 passenger seagliders annually. The first seagliders are due to be manufactured towards the end of 2027. Aside from E14, Regent’s investors include Mare Liberum, AE Ventures, Alaska Airlines, Japan Airlines and Lockheed Martin. Thalheimer approximates that 40% of the global population resides in or near coastal regions therefore there is potentially a large market for both people and goods transportation.

items.descriptionOriginal: As the primary command center of our bodies, human brains have several layers of protection to help keep them safe from dangerous invaders. Unfortunately, some of these safeguards—in particular, the blood–brain barrier (BBB)—make it hard to deliver medications to this essential organ.

items.descriptionOriginal: A bird following a boat at sea can mean a variety of things to superstitious sailors. They have been seen as harbingers of nearby land, bearers of the souls of the dead or talismans of good luck, among others. Now add this: They deliver data. A group of scientists from the United Kingdom, New Zealand and Spain have wired seabirds with tiny audio recorders and used them as unwitting boat-trackers. The recordings reveal these birds are encountering a lot more vessels on the water than regular vessel-monitoring systems show, according to a paper published today in Science Advances . That insight could help conservationists better protect endangered seabirds from getting killed by fishing nets. “For threatened seabirds,” said Jonathan Rutter , a University of Oxford scientist and the paper’s lead author. “Understanding where they encounter fishing vessels is crucial to protecting them.” Fishing boats can be a magnet for seabirds seeking an easy meal from trapped or discarded fish. But those encounters can prove lethal for animals like the Balearic shearwater , considered Europe’s most endangered seabird . Accidental capture by fishing nets or lines, commonly known as bycatch, is a prime threat to the gull-like brown bird that nests only on Spain’s Balearic Islands in the western Mediterranean Sea. That makes knowing the whereabouts of fishing boats a key part of protecting and recovering such birds. It can help scientist estimate the toll of bycatch, and whether measures such as fishing restrictions are needed. But it’s hard to know how many boats are really on the water. Most large vessels are supposed to carry transponders that continuously signal their location. But there has long been a problem with “invisible” boats, because beacons are turned off or malfunctioning, or sailors eschew the equipment altogether. .IRPP_ruby , .IRPP_ruby .postImageUrl , crisscrossed by 1000s of ships that have been virtually invisible. Until now. Some researchers have used satellites to try to solve the problem . But that doesn’t tell scientists how much birds are interacting with these boats. The advent of small, cheap audio recorders and computer programs capable of identifying the acoustic fingerprint of various animals and machines gave Rutter and colleagues another approach. They attached acoustic recorders and tracking devices to seabirds in three different parts of the ocean to see what boats they encountered. In the North Atlantic near the British Isles they used seven northern gannets. In the Mediterranean near the Spanish coast they outfitted four Balearic shearwaters. And in the south Pacific they used a lone Westland petrel. The audio recordings revealed that the birds encountered far more vessels than standard tracking data revealed. The tell-tale drone of ship equipment, compared to vessel tracking records, told the scientists that roughly 57% of the gannets’ ship encounters occurred with vessels that didn’t turn up in normal monitoring systems. For shearwaters, it was around 20%. “We know that seabirds regularly interact with fishing vessels at sea, but what surprised us was just how many of these interactions were missing from conventional tracking records,” said Rutter. The system isn’t perfect. It could be fine-tuned to better distinguish the sounds of fishing boats from other craft. And it wouldn’t work in cases where fishers string lines of hooks stretching dozens of kilometers across the water, far out of earshot of the boat. The method “is not a silver bullet,” the authors write. But it could be “a growing toolbox in which no method provides a complete picture.” So don’t expect flocks of eavesdropping birds to suddenly take to the skies. Then again, these days you never know who’s listening. Rutter et. al. “Unseen but not unheard: Animal-borne audio recorders reveal missing interactions between seabirds and untracked vessels.” Science Advances. Nov. 25, 2026. items.description: Τα πιάτα της παιδικής ηλικίας μπορούν να σας μεταφέρουν κατευθείαν στη θέση σας στο οικογενειακό τραπέζι. Τα άνετα γεύματα που σερβίρονται εκεί είναι εξαιρετικά νοσταλγικά. Και υπάρχει ένα πιάτο που αντιπροσωπεύει την επιτομή του Gen X και των παιδικών χρόνων που ξεκίνησαν το μωρό: η κατσαρόλα. Αυτά τα θαύματα ενός πιάτου ήταν γεμάτα γεύση και ψήθηκαν στην τελειότητα. Τραβιέται κατευθείαν από το φούρνο στο…
items.descriptionOriginal: Childhood dishes can take you straight back to your seat at the family dinner table. Comfort meals that were served there are uber-nostalgic. And there is one dish that represents the epitome of Gen X and baby boomer childhoods: casseroles. These one-dish wonders were loaded with flavor and baked to perfection. Pulled straight from the oven to the dinner table, casseroles filled the house with the smell of unique home-cooked recipes. And while most of us are eating casseroles today at Thanksgiving , Gen Xers and boomers grew up eating casseroles on the reg. Here are 15 old-school casserole recipes that Redditors grew up eating, which are just as yummy today: Chicken casseroles Fancy Fast Chicken casserole “ Fancy Fast Chicken is delicious and so simple. Line up chicken breasts in a casserole dish. Dump uncooked stuffing over top the chicken breasts. Pour Cream of Mushroom (Onion or chicken works too) and incorporate it into the stuffing. Top with cheese of your choice, and fried onions if you’re inclined. Bake at 350 for 45min or until chicken is thoroughly cooked.” – Applepoisoneer Chicken Curry Divan casserole “My favorite is Chicken Curry Divan. A friend made it for me in college 40 years ago and it is a favorite to this day. Never disappoints. Many people have asked me for the recipe over the years. My best friends kids now that they are grown have each approached me for it. 1 1/2 lbs chicken breast tenders cooked and cut into bite sized pieces 3 cups broccoli in bite sized pieces 2 cans Cream of Chicken soup 1 cup mayonnaise (must be Mayo) 2 tsp curry Juice of 1 lemon Shredded sharp cheddar (use the amount you like o like a nice even cover of the top) 3/4 cup crushed Ritz crackers 3 tbsp melted butter In 9×13” baking pan layer chicken then broccoli. Mix the soup, Mayo, lemon juice and curry together well, pour over chicken broccoli mixture evenly and smooth out. Sprinkle cheese over top evenly. Crush crackers fine, mix in melted butter well and sprinkle evenly over top. Cook at 375° for 25-30 minutes until bubbly and top brown. Serve with rice.” – karinchup Chicken and Rice casserole “This baked rice & cheese casserole has become a staple in our house! It’s great as a side dish, or I’ll add rotisserie chicken and serve it as a main dish.” – anchovypepperonitoni Chicken & Dumplings casserole “The secret of this is not to stir anything. That’s what makes your dumplings. When you dish it out, you have your dumplings on top. 2 chicken breasts, cooked and shredded; 2 cups chicken broth; 1/2 stick of butter; 2 cups Bisquick mix; 2 cups whole milk; 1 can cream of chicken soup; 1/2 medium onion, minced; 1 cup frozen peas; 3 tsp chicken Better Than Bouillon; 1/2 tsp dried sage; 1 tsp black pepper; 1/2 tsp salt. (1) Preheat oven to 350 degrees (2) Layer 1 – In 9×13 casserole dish, melt 1/2 stick of butter. Spread shredded chicken over butter. Sprinkle black pepper and dried sage over this layer. Do not stir. (3) Layer 2 – Sprinkle minced onions and peas over chicken (4) Layer 3 – In small bowl, mix milk and Bisquick. Slowly pour all over chicken. Do not stir. (5) Layer 4 – In medium bowl, whisk together 2 cups of chicken broth, chicken bouillon, and soup. Once blended, slowly pour over the Bisquick layer. Do not stir. (6) Bake casserole for 30-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown.” – Superb_Yak7074 Chicken broccoli casserole “I made chicken broccoli casserole last week and that’s a favorite here. This is pretty close to how I do it.” – gimmethelulz Potato casseroles Funeral Potatoes “The unfortunately named, funeral potatoes !” – IRLperson Tater Tot casserole “ Tater tot casserole . My mom made this at least once a week when I was growing up, but she added a quart of green beans to make it a meal. If you brown your ground beef in a good size cast iron skillet, you only dirty up one pan to make it!” – hcynthia1234, upperwareParTAY Breakfast casserole “I’m making a breakfast casserole this morning for brunch later, a bag of frozen hash brown potatoes thawed, a pound of sausage sauteed with peppers and onions, a brick of cheese grated, eight eggs beaten with a bit of milk and cream and some salt and pepper. Layer in a casserole, ending with cheese. Bake around an hour at 375.” – CWrend Hamburger pie casserole “One of my childhood favorites . Did not add vegetables or cheese though. This was an end of the month struggle meal that everyone loved.” – DarnHeather Shepherd’s pie casserole “Shepherd’s pie : brown 1.5 lbs ground beef with half a chopped onion, salt and pepper, drain it and then spread into a 13×9 and stir a can of cream of mushroom soup into it. Spread a drained family size can of corn on top, use a container of prepared mashed potatoes for the top layer. Bake for a half hour at 350.” – ExplanationLucky1143 Noodle casseroles Tuna casserole “Love my mom’s tuna noodle casserole: 1 bag broad egg noodles, 1 can cream of mushroom soup, 2 cans tuna, 1 cup frozen corn or 1 can kernel corn, 2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese, 1/2 cup seasoned bread crumbs, 1 tbsp celery salt Cook noodles per package directions, drain, then place in a 13×9 casserole dish. Mix in cream of mushroom soup, tuna, corn, 1 cup of the cheddar cheese, and celery salt. Top the casserole with the remaining cheese and bread crumbs. Bake at 350 for 20 minutes or until done enough for you.” – Pinkleton Mock Stroganoff casserole “Mock stroganoff – brown 1lb ground chuck. Mix in 8 oz sour cream and 1 can cream of mushroom. Add to 1 lb of cooked egg noodles. Season with black pepper. Extras – fresh mushrooms and/or onion cooked with the beef. Any precooked veggies of your choice, peas or broccoli work well. Splash of Worcestershire, soy sauce, or fish sauce. Garlic or onion powder. Parsley, thyme, or cilantro.” – Nathan_Saul Cabbage noodle casserole “I have a quick cabbage and noodles that uses bagged cole slaw. Cook a bag of noodles. Put aside. Cut up a lb of bacon and a med onion. Cook in pan until bacon is slightly fried and onions are clear. Add cabbage(without carrots) let sit 10 min or so. Add to noodles. It’s so easy.” – conjas11 Vegetable casseroles Green bean casserole “ This is the best green bean casserole recipe, it does use the canned onions but you make your own cream of mushroom and it’s soooo good. I’ve made it on random weekends, it’s not just a Thanksgiving food. I don’t know much about older foods, I just really wanted to share that recipe.” Corn casserole “Our family Corn custard doesn’t have crackers but we double the recipe and there’s never any left over. 2 eggs, 1 cup of sweetened condensed milk, 1/2 flour, 2 T soft butter, 1 tsp sugar, 1 can of creamed corn, 1 can of whole corn. Mix all together and bake in a 8×8 about 45 min at 350. Gotta have that!” – Psychological_Bat890 What are your easy casserole week night recipes by u/arifirari in Old_Recipes Casseroles still have a spot at the table Casseroles started as budget-friendly dinners, but they stuck around because they work: one dish, simple ingredients, and enough to feed everyone. For many Gen Xers and boomers, they also taste like childhood. Thanksgiving is this Thursday, so there’s a good chance one of these recipes will make it onto your table, whether it’s the green bean classic or a pan of funeral potatoes. Which casserole did you grow up eating? Tell us in the comments. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post 15 old-school casserole recipes that feel like home for boomers and Gen Xers appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: If you’ve ever tried to make a cat do something it doesn’t want to do, you’ve likely experienced the terror that a cat’s wrath can invoke. Our cute, cuddly feline friends may be small, but the razor blades on their feet are no joke when they decide to utilize them. Even cats who love us can get spicy if we try to manhandle them , so we can imagine how things will go with cats who don’t know us well. But sometimes it’s necessary to handle a cat even if it’s resistant to the idea. This is where Vancouver veterinarian Dr. Uri Burstyn comes in. His “How to pick up a cat like a pro” video , in which he demonstrates a few ways of picking up and handling a cat, has been viewed over 23 million times since he shared it in 2018. Unlike many viral videos, it’s not humorous and nothing outrageous happens, but the combo of Burstyn’s calm demeanor and his repeated instructions to “squish that cat” has endeared him to the masses . The video truly is helpful; he shows the ways to pick up a cat that make them feel the most secure using his cats, Claudia (then 1 year old) and Mr. Pirate (then 14). He explains that cats spook very easily and it’s best to introduce yourself to them gently. Let them sniff your fingers, keeping your fingers curled in, and once they’ve sniffed you, you can often give them a light rub on the cheek or under the chin. Why cats scratch when you pick them up Picking them up is a different story. The reason many cats will claw or scratch you when you try to pick them up is because they feel unsupported or unsafe , so they’ll scramble around trying to get some footing. Burstyn shows how he picks up Claudia with one hand under the chest and one hand under her abdomen. If he needs to carry her around, he squishes her into his body so she feels “nice and supported .” He may even put a hand under her front paws. Cats can be finicky about how they’re held. Photo credit: Canva Then came the best part of the video: “Squish That Cat” “Now if we do have a cat who’s trying to get away from us?” Burstyn said. “We always squish that cat. If you’re trying to hold the cat down, whether it’s to trim their nails or to give them a pill , or whether you just want to have a cat not run off for a moment, squish that cat. All you need to know about cat restraint is to squish that cat.” Burstyn explains that cats generally feel very secure being squished, even if they’re really scared. “Sometimes cats come to me in the clinic, and they’re quite afraid,” he said. “And you just gently squish them, and they’ll sit there and kind of not hurt themselves, not hurt us. Just hang out and let us do our thing.” He demonstrated putting a towel over the cat, explaining, “If you have a towel handy, this is one of the best cat restraint tools around. You can just throw a towel on the catty and squish her with the towel, that way they won’t get a claw into you if they are scrambling about a bit. Very safe and gentle, and generally cats are very, very happy to be squished like that.” The fastest way to carry a cat safely Dr. Burstyn also showed how to do a “football carry,” tucking the cat under your arm with them facing backwards. “So this is kind of an emergency way if you really need to carry a cat somewhere in a hurry,” he said. Scooping up Claudia, he explained, “Little head’s under your arm, butt in your hand, and you squish her tight to your body. And with that little football carry, you can basically hold a cat very securely and very safely, because it’s really hard for them to rake you with their hind legs.” If you’re worried about over-squishing your cat, Dr. Burstyn says don’t. “You don’t have to worry about hurting a cat,” he said. “They’re very, very tough little beasts. You know, just squishing them against your body’s never going to do them any harm. In fact, they tend to feel more safe and secure when they’re being held tightly.” Dr. Burstyn also demonstrated how to pick up and set down a “shoulder cat” who insists on climbing onto people’s shoulders and hanging out there, as Mr. Pirate does. It’s highly entertaining, as Mr. Pirate is a big ol’ chonky kitty. The internet couldn’t get enough People in the comments loved Dr. Burstyn’s demonstration, with several dubbing him the Bob Ross of veterinary medicine. Even people who don’t have cats said they watched the whole video, and many loved Claudia and Mr. Pirate as well. “This is just proof that cats are liquid.” “12/10 cat. Excellent squishability.” “So essentially, cats love hugs? That’s the most wonderful thing i’ve heard all day.” “This cat is so well mannered and looks educated.” “Mr Pirate is an absolute unit.” “S q u i s h . T h a t . C a t .” “I need ‘Squish that cat’ shirt.” “Dang, that actually helped with my female cat. She has been through at least two owners before me and had some bad experiences which obviously resulted in trust issues. She has now been with me for two years and it had gotten loads better, but she still did not want me to hold her. Normally I simply would have let her be, but for vet visits and such it was not an ideal situation. But then I saw this video and tried to squish the cat. And she loves it! She is turning into quite the snuggly bug. Thank you!” So there you go. When all else fails, squish that cat and see what happens. You can follow Dr. Burstyn on YouTube at Helpful Vancouver Vet . This article originally appeared in February. It has been updated. The post Vet demonstrates ‘squish the cat’ method of safe cat handling in delightfully helpful video appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: The hidden digital detail inside Taylor Swift’s wedding invitations designed to catch guests who leaked it
items.description: Η Taylor Swift και ο αστέρας του NFL, Travis Kelce, πέρασαν το μεγαλύτερο μέρος του έτους σχεδιάζοντας τη γαμήλια εκδήλωση του αιώνα. Στις 3 Ιουλίου, το Σαββατοκύριακο της 4ης Ιουλίου, η παγκοσμίου φήμης τραγουδίστρια και το tight end των Kansas City Chiefs το έκαναν επίσημο. Αντάλλαξαν όρκους μέσα σε ένα μεταμορφωμένο Madison Square Garden, με τον Adam Sandler να ιερουργεί. Δείτε αυτήν την ανάρτηση στο Instagra…
items.descriptionOriginal: Taylor Swift and NFL star Travis Kelce spent the better part of a year planning the wedding event of the century. On July 3, over Fourth of July weekend, the world-famous singer and Kansas City Chiefs tight end made it official. They exchanged vows inside a transformed Madison Square Garden, with Adam Sandler officiating. View this post on Instagram High-profile nuptials are nothing new, but the fact that the couple pulled off a massive, star-studded ceremony with nearly 1,000 attendees in the heart of Manhattan without paparazzi spoiling the big moment? Well, that required some ingenuity. The first step? Sending out the wedding invitations . The invites had details the couple wanted to keep private from the prying eyes of the public and the press. In typical Swift fashion, Taylor combined personal passion with a dash of technology to pull off the perfect wedding announcement. A portrait in pop star privacy The invite featured a lush forest scene and an orange sky complemented by a custom heart-wrapped, double “T” monogram. On social media, Swifties pushed the idea that Taylor had painted the gorgeous woodland landscape herself since she had worked in watercolors in the past. To orchestrate this stealth ceremony, Swift blended old-school artistry with a digital trap. Each wedding invitation had a hidden watermark embedded with the recipient’s name . If the invitee tried to leak the private details, Taylor would be able to track down the culprit. Three days before the ceremony, it happened. Ashish Ferguson, brother of Travis’ childhood pal and personal chef, posted the invite online briefly before he took it down. It was an open-and-shut case, too, since Swift fans instantly spied his name in the watercolor background. It looked good… and a little too good to be true To make a wedding like this happen without everyone watching requires monumental effort and a little bit of subterfuge. BBC Radio 1 host Greg James revealed on his breakfast show that he received the invitation link unexpectedly in the middle of the night. Since it lacked traditional paper stationery, James admitted he and his wife spent weeks wondering if the message was genuine or a highly sophisticated internet phishing scam. James told his audience that he wasn’t completely convinced that they had been officially invited until they crossed the threshold of Madison Square Garden. “Until we were in, we were like, ‘We might have made a big trip for nothing here.'” Ultimately, Taylor’s defensive measures worked brilliantly. Despite the one blink-and-you’ll-miss-it leak and a bit of guest confusion, the nuptials reportedly went off without a hitch. This article originally appeared in July. It has been updated. The post The hidden digital detail inside Taylor Swift’s wedding invitations designed to catch guests who leaked it appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Το έργο επιστημονικής έκθεσης για μαθητή της 6ης δημοτικού απαντά στην παλαιά ερώτηση: «Αγγίζουν τα πάντα οι οπίσθιες τρύπες της γάτας;»
items.titleOriginal: 6th grader’s science fair project answers age-old question: ‘Do cat buttholes touch everything?’
items.description: Οι ιδιοκτήτες γατών είναι μια ιδιαίτερη φυλή ανθρώπων. Μερικές φορές, όταν συναλλάσσονται με φίλους αιλουροειδών , έχουν μοναδικές ερωτήσεις στις οποίες ακόμη και η Google δεν έχει πάντα την απάντηση. Αυτός είναι πιθανώς ο μόνος λόγος που υπάρχουν τα φόρουμ για γάτες, αλλά ένα παιδί που χρειαζόταν ένα επιστημονικό έργο στην 6η τάξη αποφάσισε να παραλείψει τα φόρουμ για τις γάτες για απαντήσεις και αντ' αυτού να χρησιμοποιήσει την επιστημονική μέθοδο. Κ…
items.descriptionOriginal: Cat owners are a special breed of people. Sometimes, in dealing with feline friends , they have unique questions that even Google doesn’t always have the answer to. This is probably the sole reason cat forums exist, but one kid who needed a 6th grade science project decided to skip the cat forums for answers and instead use the scientific method. Kaeden Henry, then a sixth grader living in Florida, bravely pondered a question few (if any) have been brave enough to ask: do cat buttholes touch every surface they sit on? Since cats do whatever the heck they want , training them not to jump on kitchen counters is a feat even Hercules struggles to complete. These fierce felines don’t care if you’re cooking dinner or trying to get comfy in bed. If they want to sit somewhere, they’re going to do it. The thought of cat butts on that expensive Serta pillow designed to feel like you’re sleeping on a cloud can gross people out, but thanks to Kaeden, you no longer have to wonder if the butthole itself is also making contact. The scientific method as it was meant to be used. Courtesy of Kerry Hyde The curious sixth grader was homeschooled and well-versed in the scientific method thanks to his mother’s PhD in animal behavior with a concentration in feline behavior. And, since they own cats, the science experiment was pretty straightforward (and directly impactful). How the lipstick experiment worked To complete the experiment, Henry and his mom, Kerry Hyde, bought non-toxic lipstick and applied it to each of their cats’ anuses. Then, the cats were given commands. (Commands… hilarious, right?) “Non-toxic lipstick was applied to their bum-bums, they were then given a series of commands (sit, wait, lie down, and jump up. Side note: Both cats have been trained since kittenhood with a variety of commands, they also know how to high-five, spin around, and speak.), they were compensated with lots of praise, pets, and their favorite treats, and the lipstick was removed with a baby wipe once we collected our data in just under 10 minutes,” Hyde wrote in a Facebook post. The results? In this small home experiment with two cats, no, cat buttholes did not touch every surface they sat on. Now, let’s all take a collective sigh of relief while we go over the details. Kaeden’s experiment compared a short-haired cat with a longer-haired one (if your cat is hairless, you’d better stock up on Clorox wipes just in case). “His results and general findings: Long and medium haired cat’s buttholes made NO contact with soft or hard surfaces at all. Short haired cats made NO contact on hard surfaces. But we did see evidence of a slight smear on the soft bedding surface. Conclusion, if you have a short haired cat and they may be lying on a pile of laundry, an unmade bed, or other soft uneven surface, then their butthole MAY touch those surfaces!” Hyde shares. Now every curious cat owner can rest easy knowing that as long as their cat has hair, their bare bottom balloon knot is not touching the majority of surfaces in their home. High five for an A+! Courtesy of Kerry Hyde There was no shortage of comments The amusing experiment caught the internet’s attention. People laughed and commented, with one person writing, “This is probably the most useful information I’ve learned from a science fair project.” “Good to know!…I can now eat my sandwich left on the counter with confidence!” another writes. “A+++!!! Whew!! I am very grateful for your sciencing on this subject. My fears from walking in on my cat sitting on my laptop keyboard and subsequently being grossed out and cleaning furiously in a hyper-ocd manner have been somewhat allayed and now maybe I won’t have to use QUIIITE so many wipes,” someone chimes in. “Finally.. Someone answers the important questions!!” Cat butthole knowledge is power So the next time your cat plops down on your favorite pillow, you can breathe a little easier. Kaeden set out to answer a question most cat owners have quietly wondered about, and he did it with a little lipstick, two well-trained cats and a whole lot of curiosity. The best part of the story? Kaeden’s mom has a PhD in animal behavior, specializing in feline behavior, and even she learned something new. The power of science! This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post 6th grader’s science fair project answers age-old question: ‘Do cat buttholes touch everything?’ appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: Μια εταιρεία χυμών πέταξε φλούδες πορτοκαλιού σε ένα εθνικό πάρκο. Έτσι μοιάζει σήμερα.
items.titleOriginal: A juice company dumped orange peels in a national park. This is what it looks like today.
items.description: Το 1997, οι οικολόγοι Daniel Janzen και Winnie Hallwachs προσέγγισαν μια εταιρεία χυμού πορτοκαλιού στην Κόστα Ρίκα με την επωνυμία Del Oro με μια ιδέα που δεν ήταν άγνωστη. Σε αντάλλαγμα για τη δωρεά μιας μερίδας παρθένας, δασικής γης στην Área de Conservación Guanacaste, ένα φυσικό καταφύγιο στα βορειοδυτικά της χώρας, το πάρκο θα επέτρεπε στην εταιρεία να απορρίψει τα απορριπτέα του.…
items.descriptionOriginal: In 1997, ecologists Daniel Janzen and Winnie Hallwachs approached an orange juice company in Costa Rica called Del Oro with an off-the-wall idea . In exchange for donating a portion of unspoiled, forested land to the Área de Conservación Guanacaste, a nature preserve in the country’s northwest, the park would allow the company to dump its discarded orange peels and pulp, free of charge, in a heavily grazed, largely deforested area nearby. One year later, one thousand trucks poured into the national park, offloading over 12,000 metric tons of sticky, mealy, orange compost onto the worn-out plot. The project was forced to end after just its second year, though, when rival juice manufacturer TicoFrut sued Del Oro, alleging it had defiled a national park, and Costa Rica’s Supreme Court ultimately sided with the plaintiff. The site was left untouched and largely unexamined for over a decade. Finding the site years later on Sixteen years later, Janzen dispatched graduate student Timothy Treuer to look for the site where the food waste was dumped. Treuer initially set out to locate the large placard that marked the plot, and failed. The first deposit of orange peels in 1997. Photo by Dan Janzen. “It’s a huge sign, bright yellow lettering. We should have been able to see it,” Treuer says. After wandering around for half an hour with no luck, he consulted Janzen, who gave him more detailed instructions on how to find the plot. When he returned a week later and confirmed he was in the right place, Treuer was floored. Compared to the adjacent barren former pastureland, the site of the food waste deposit was “like night and day.” The site of the orange peel deposit (L) and adjacent pastureland (R). Photo by Leland Werden. “It was just hard to believe that the only difference between the two areas was a bunch of orange peels. They look like completely different ecosystems,” he explains. The area was so thick with vegetation he still could not find the sign. Treuer and a team of researchers from Princeton University studied the site over the course of the following three years. What the researchers discovered The results, published in the journal “Restoration Ecology ,” highlight just how completely the discarded fruit parts assisted the area’s turnaround. According to the Princeton School of Public and International Affairs, the experiment resulted in a “176 percent increase in aboveground biomass, or the wood in the trees, within the 3-hectare area (7 acres) studied.” The ecologists measured various qualities of the site against an area of former pastureland immediately across the access road used to dump the orange peels two decades prior. Compared to the adjacent plot, which was dominated by a single species of tree, the site of the orange peel deposit featured two dozen species of vegetation, most thriving. Lab technician Erik Schilling explores the newly overgrown orange peel plot. Photo by Tim Treuer. In addition to greater biodiversity, richer soil, and a better-developed canopy, researchers discovered a tayra (a dog-sized weasel) and a giant fig tree three feet in diameter, on the plot. “You could have had 20 people climbing in that tree at once and it would have supported the weight no problem,” says Jon Choi, co-author of the paper, who conducted much of the soil analysis. “That thing was massive.” Why this matters for the climate Research suggests that secondary tropical forests, those that grow after the original inhabitants are torn down, are essential to helping slow climate change. In a 2016 study published in Nature, researchers found that such forests absorb and store atmospheric carbon at roughly 11 times the rate of old-growth forests. Treuer believes better management of discarded produce, like orange peels, could be key to helping these forests regrow. In many parts of the world, rates of deforestation are increasing dramatically, sapping local soil of much-needed nutrients and, with them, the ability of ecosystems to restore themselves. Meanwhile, much of the world is awash in nutrient-rich food waste. In the United States, up to half of all produce in the United States is discarded. Most currently ends up in landfills. The site after a deposit of orange peels in 1998. Photo by Dan Janzen. “We don’t want companies to go out there willy-nilly just dumping their waste all over the place, but if it’s scientifically driven and restorationists are involved in addition to companies, this is something I think has really high potential,” Treuer says. The next step, he believes, is to examine whether other ecosystems such as dry forests, cloud forests and tropical savannas react the same way to similar deposits. Two years after his initial survey, Treuer returned to once again try to locate the sign marking the site. Since his first scouting mission in 2013, Treuer had visited the plot more than 15 times. Choi had visited more than 50. Neither had spotted the original sign. In 2015, when Treuer, with the help of the paper’s senior author, David Wilcove, and Princeton Professor Rob Pringle, finally found it under a thicket of vines, the scope of the area’s transformation became truly clear. “It’s a big honking sign,” Choi emphasizes. The sign after clearing away the vines. Photo by Tim Treuer. A sign worth waiting for Seventeen years had passed since that first truckload of peels rolled in, long enough for a barren pasture to become an unrecognizable forest, and long enough to bury even a seven-foot sign under a thicket of vines. All it took was two scientists, a flash of inspiration, and the humble rind of an orange to prove that sometimes the best solutions really are hiding in plain sight, or in this case, under a few decades of undergrowth. The orange peel experiment was never meant to run this long, or to prove quite this much. But Janzen and Hallwachs’ willingness to try something unconventional turned a legal dead end into one of the most compelling case studies for low-cost forest restoration on record. Sometimes the smallest, strangest ideas end up growing into the biggest ones. This article originally appeared ten years ago. It has been updated. The post A juice company dumped orange peels in a national park. This is what it looks like today. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Από υφάσματα υψηλής απόκρισης που δημιουργούν μια νέα εμπειρία αφής στο gaming έως διαδραστικές οθόνες, μαλακούς ρομποτικούς βραχίονες και έξυπνα εργοστασιακά συστήματα μεταφοράς—μικροσκοπικά ρομπότ κατασκευασμένα από λεπτές μεμβράνες πολυμερούς θα μπορούσαν να παρέχουν στις επιφάνειες μια ολόκληρη σειρά νέων και χρήσιμων λειτουργιών. Η ερευνητική ομάδα του καθηγητή Gianluca Rizzello στο Πανεπιστήμιο του Saarland μελετά…
items.descriptionOriginal: From responsive textiles that create a new tactile experience in gaming to interactive displays, soft robotic arms and intelligent factory conveyor systems—miniature robots made from thin polymer films could provide surfaces with a whole range of new and useful functions. Professor Gianluca Rizzello's research group at Saarland University is studying how such film-based robots work together beneath a silicone skin, acting collectively like artificial muscles and sensory nerves. Lightweight, flexible and powered solely by electricity, the system requires no bulky hydraulic or pneumatic equipment, external sensors, cameras or tangles of cables.

Η λύση…
items.descriptionOriginal: Chinese firm Gaotu Innovation has developed a portable, fold-out solar solution for electric-vehicle drivers, designed to be fitted to a car and used outside Australia’s existing charging infrastructure. The company claims it can harness solar energy, then store and use that electricity independently of any connection to the national grid. The solution includes folding solar panels and an internal 2.5kWh lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) battery, and it can achieve a maximum solar power intake of 1,600W. Gaotu claims that, depending on factors including solar availability, panel orientation and vehicle power requirements, this can provide enough electricity to cover a distance of up to 50 miles (80km) per day. The battery is not part of a vehicle’s primary traction battery, it is used to store the solar energy harvested by the panels. An internal charger then uses power electronics to distribute this power. While a car is stationary, the panels can be unfurled so they continue absorbing solar energy and recharging the system. Gaotu is promoting the system to Australian drivers, for example those who wish to drive in more outback areas, stay at more secluded sites and/or frequently drive where public charging stations are not easily accessible. Fold-out panels deliver 1,600W solar input The GT-EV16-PB-FD contains two maximum power point tracking (MPPT) controllers. Each can accept a solar power input of 800W, giving a total maximum of 1,600W. Gaotu claims the MPPT controllers are 99.9% efficient and the solar cells are 25% efficient. Once harvested, solar electricity is sent to the internal 2.5kWh battery, which distributes it to a vehicle and also helps stabilize the solar supply. Alternating current (AC) power is distributed via the charger . Owners can use a smartphone app, along with Bluetooth and Wi-Fi connectivity to the device, to view and control the charging process, removing the need to interact with the device directly. The fold-out solar panels are housed in a case with an IP68 sealing standard. Alongside its streamlined shape, Gaotu says the device is robust and able to endure winds of up to around 100mph (160km/h). It is suitable for temperatures between -4°F and 131°F. 10ms backup power for emergencies In addition to charging, the device can also serve as an off-grid uninterruptible power supply (UPS). Should there be an outage in a vehicle’s primary power source; it can supply secondary power to devices. Gaotu claims it can begin distributing secondary power just 10 milliseconds after a primary power source is cut off. This may benefit those staying in isolated areas or places without easy access to steady power. Gaotu states that the power supplied by the system falls by around 1% in the first year and then by a maximum of 0.4% in following years. These are manufacturer’s indicative figures. Gaotu provides a five-year craftsmanship warranty and a two-year power performance warranty. It also intends to export fully assembled systems to Australian local distributors. Original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM) adaptations can be requested by commercial partners. As noted, this approximate 50-mile per day figure depends on solar availability, installation and the vehicle’s power requirements.

items.descriptionOriginal: Σοβαρό περιστατικό τραυματισμού 11χρονου μαθητή σημειώθηκε έξω από το Δημοτικό Σχολείο Αρφαρών στη Μεσσηνία , όταν ένας 10χρονος συμμαθητής του φέρεται να τον έσπρωξε, με αποτέλεσμα να πέσει πάνω στα κάγκελα του σχολείου και να τραυματιστεί σοβαρά στο κεφάλι. Το παιδί μεταφέρθηκε αρχικά στο Νοσοκομείο Καλαμάτας και στη συνέχεια στο Νοσοκομείο Παίδων στην Αθήνα, όπου εξακολουθεί να νοσηλεύεται. Το περιστατικό σημειώθηκε το μεσημέρι της Τρίτης, την ώρα που οι μαθητές αποχωρούσαν από το σχολείο μετά τη λήξη των μαθημάτων. Σύμφωνα με τις πληροφορίες, ο 10χρονος έσπρωξε τον 11χρονο συμμαθητή του, ο οποίος έχασε την ισορροπία του και προσέκρουσε στα κάγκελα της σχολικής εγκατάστασης. Σύμφωνα με το patrisnews.com, από την πτώση ο 11χρονος υπέστη τραύμα στο κεφάλι και μεταφέρθηκε εσπευσμένα στο Νοσοκομείο Καλαμάτας. Εκεί οι γιατροί τού έκαναν ράμματα, ενώ στη συνέχεια κρίθηκε απαραίτητη, για προληπτικούς λόγους, η διακομιδή του σε Νοσοκομείο Παίδων της Αθήνας, όπου παραμένει υπό νοσηλεία. Μετά τον τραυματισμό του παιδιού, η μητέρα του υπέβαλε μήνυση στις αρμόδιες Αρχές. Στο πλαίσιο της υπόθεσης συνελήφθη η 51χρονη μητέρα του 10χρονου μαθητή , σε βάρος της οποίας σχηματίστηκε δικογραφία για επικίνδυνη σωματική βλάβη και παραμέληση εποπτείας ανηλίκου. Την προανάκριση για τις συνθήκες κάτω από τις οποίες σημειώθηκε το περιστατικό διενεργεί η Υποδιεύθυνση Δίωξης και Εξιχνίασης Εγκλημάτων Καλαμάτας, ενώ έχει παραγγελθεί και ιατροδικαστική εξέταση για τον τραυματισμό του 11χρονου. Ειδήσεις σήμερα «Μαζί στην πρώτη γραμμή»: Άσκηση από την ΕΛΑΣ και τη 2η ΥΠΕ για την αντιμετώπιση της ενδοοικογενειακής βίας Βία κατά των γυναικών: Οδηγίες προστασίας και στήριξη από τον Ελληνικό Ερυθρό Σταυρό Στο ΚΑΤ η Χριστίνα Βακάκη: Χειρουργείται στον αγκώνα μετά την παράσυρσή της από ΙΧ

items.title: Τρακτέρ κυψελών καυσίμου υδρογόνου με δεξαμενές 350 bar θα μπορούσε να μειώσει τη χρήση ορυκτών καυσίμων στη γεωργία
items.titleOriginal: Hydrogen fuel cell tractor with 350-bar tanks could slash fossil fuel use in farming
items.description: Ερευνητές στη Γερμανία ανακάλυψαν έναν ελκυστήρα κυψελών καυσίμου υδρογόνου εξοπλισμένου με δεξαμενές 350 bar και επί του παρόντος δοκιμάζουν εάν μπορεί να αντικαταστήσει τους τρακτέρ ντίζελ και να μειώσει τις εκπομπές ρύπων από τη γεωργία. items.descriptionOriginal: Researchers in Germany have invented a hydrogen fuel cell tractor equipped with 350-bar tanks, and are currently testing whether it can replace diesel tractors and reduce emissions from farming. Dubbed H2tofielddrive, the project is carried out by scientists at the University of Bonn. Its goal is to evaluate one of Germany’s first hydrogen fuel cell tractors and determine whether it could be used in everyday farming. To overcome the refueling challenges, the team also acquired a mobile hydrogen station that operates at a pressure of 500 bar. The station supplies hydrogen to the university’s research farm without the need for fixed refueling facilities. Jürgen Rath, PhD, a researcher from the University of Bonn said that the team will now assess the tractor’s energy efficiency and performance, and examine what is needed to use hydrogen-powered machinery. “The energy efficiency of hydrogen compared to conventional fossil fuels in agricultural tractors is being investigated as part of a doctoral research project at the University of Bonn,” he added. Running on hydrogen According to the team, refueling the tractor posed a massive challenge at first. Its hydrogen tanks operate at aa pressure of 350 bar (5,076 pounds per square inch). So, to refuel it without an additional compressor, they needed a hydrogen supply at a higher pressure. To tackle the matter, energy supplier Knauber secured access to hydrogen at the required pressure through its network and took responsibility for the logistics of the hydrogen supply . The mobile station acquired by the university operates at 500 bar (7,252 pounds per square inch). Refueling the hydrogen fuel cell tractor with the mobile hydrogen station. Credit: Campus Klein-Altendorf / Uni Bonn Rath explained that the trailer-like mobile station brings hydrogen directly to the testing site at the university’s Klein-Altendorf campus. The tractor can, hence, be refueled without a permanent refueling station. However, mobile refueling solutions remain relatively scarce in the country, which their implementation a technical and logistical challenge. “The development of a hydrogen economy requires not only innovative applications but also the right infrastructure,” Mortiz Kroymann, Knauber sales manager, said. “Projects like this provide important insights into the future use of hydrogen in agriculture.” A cleaner alternative The initiative is being carried out at the university’s Chair of Renewable Resources as part of an interdisciplinary doctoral study. The team pointed out that hydrogen fuel cells generate electricity through a reaction between hydrogen and oxygen. The process produces water and heat and does not release carbon dioxide (CO2). However, the fuel’s environmental footprint depends on how it is produced and delivered. The researchers will now collect empirical data on the tractor’s energy efficiency and performance and compare its efficiency with that of conventional fossil fuel-powered tractors. The hydrogen-powered tractor alongside conventional agricultural machinery. Credit: Campus Klein-Altendorf / Uni Bonn At the same time, they will test several practical aspects of hydrogen adoption in agriculture, among which infrastructure, fuel supply logistics, regulatory permits, and everyday operating procedures. “In this context, it was important for us to find a regional partner who could not only supply hydrogen but also understand the project’s specific requirements,” Rath concluded in a press statement . “This is an important factor in the project’s continued progress.”

items.description: Οι διαφορές μεταξύ της ευρωπαϊκής κουλτούρας και της αμερικανικής κουλτούρας δεν παύουν να μας εκπλήσσουν (και να μας διασκεδάζουν). items.descriptionOriginal: The differences between European culture and American culture never cease to surprise (and entertain) us. From toilet preferences to personality traits , Americans do many things in distinct ways. And actor Kieran Culkin recently shared a funny cultural realization that happened between him and his British wife, Jazz Charton. In a new interview with JOE , Culkin was asked about Charton’s “Britishisms”. And he opened up about one major difference between British and American bedrooms that surprised him. Kieran Culkin says he thought his British wife was lying when she told him people in England don't use top sheets on their beds "There's also things that she'll say it's because of where she's from. And I'm like, I actually don't know if you're just saying this or if this is… pic.twitter.com/1QSbiWaCDd — Casper (@CasperOnChain) November 22, 2026 The surprising American bedroom habit During the sit-down interview with JOE , Culkin shared that there’s “always some new thing” that Charton points out is odd to her about American culture. Most recently, it was something in American bedrooms. “She hates a [top] sheet on a bed,” he explained. “She’s like, ‘It should [just] be a duvet. In England, we only do the duvet. We don’t do the sheet’.” At first, he didn’t see her point—but then he did. “So I thought, she was full of sh*t!” he added. “She kept saying, ‘Why are these always bunched up? Why are they always tossed up? They’re on the floor.’ She goes, ‘Cuz we don’t have these in England. It’s a stupid f*cking thing in a bed.’ And then I’ve since asked, and it’s a thing.” Now, he totally agrees with her. “Yeah, we’ve done away with it. She’s absolutely right. Why do we do this in America? I was like, is it to keep the duvet clean? Wash your duvet,” Culkin said enthusiastically. The top sheet sparks debate On X , people shared their impassioned opinions on whether they were pro-top sheet or against it. Pro-top sheet “Because you don’t always want the duvet. Something about a nice cool clean sheet atop your body especially if you get hot easily. Keeps you warm enough until later in night and you want to pull the duvet over.” “It’s a nightmare to get a duvet back on a comforter. Would rather use a sheet and wash it fewer times.” “So I can wash my sheet once a week and my duvet cover once a month.” “OK. As an American expat I think I have insight into this. In the US, most people have ‘comforters’ that are heavy like a duvet and cumbersome to launder, and the top sheet makes it so you don’t have to launder too often-also they are a ‘cover’ on hot summer nights when you wouldn’t dream of laying under a comforter. In the UK and Ireland there are plain white duvets for which you buy sets with matching duvet covers, fitted sheet (sometimes) and pillow cases. When you change/launder your sheets, this includes the duvet cover. For the most part, it doesn’t get hot enough that you don’t need your duvet.” Anti-top sheet “Every duvet is inside a sheet – a duvet cover that ties into the corners of the duvet. You strip the duvet cover and wash that.” “Americans sound like babies when piss on about top sheets and comforters. A duvet is adequate all year round.” “I don’t do a top sheet either. It’s annoying and useless.” “I’d never even heard of a top sheet until now. Wtf is the point of that.” The post Kieran Culkin says his wife’s very British hot take on the ‘useless’ American top sheet blew his mind appeared first on Upworthy .

items.description: Ο Henry Winkler πέρασε 11 σεζόν παίζοντας έναν από τους πιο κουλ χαρακτήρες της τηλεόρασης. items.descriptionOriginal: Henry Winkler spent 11 seasons playing one of television’s coolest characters. Originally given a minor role on Happy Days , Arthur Fonzarelli became one of the show’s biggest stars. As confident as the Fonz appeared on screen, some of Winkler’s most uncomfortable moments came before the cameras even started rolling. As Winkler explained in a 2023 interview with PBS NewsHour , he struggled to read scripts because of dyslexia , a learning disability he wasn’t diagnosed with until he was 31. By then, Winkler had developed his own techniques for getting through auditions and learning his lines. Henry Winkler on stage at 2018 Supercon. Photo Credit: Super Festivals/ Wikimedia Commons/ CC BY 2.0 (cropped) How Henry Winkler got through his auditions Winkler graduated from the Yale School of Drama in 1970 with a master’s degree, but getting through auditions presented a particular challenge. Actors are often asked to read unfamiliar material during an audition. For Winkler, this meant demonstrating his ability to play a character while struggling to read the dialogue. Speaking to The Yale Center for Dyslexia & Creativity , he explained how he would quickly memorize as much of the script as possible and improvise the portions he couldn’t remember. “You learn to negotiate with your learning challenge,” said Winkler. “I could instantly memorize a lot of it and then what I didn’t know, I made up and threw caution to the wind and did it with conviction and sometimes I made them laugh and sometimes I got hired,” he added. In a 2019 interview with NPR , Winkler recalled producers and directors pointing out that he wasn’t saying the words they had written. “I’m giving you the essence of the character,” he would tell them. The Fonz and Richie Cunningham. Photo Credit: ABC Television/ Wikimedia Commons Monday morning on the set of ‘Happy Days’ Getting the part didn’t put an end to Winkler’s difficulties with scripts. In his 2023 memoir, Being Henry: The Fonz… and Beyond , excerpted by Variety , Winkler recalled the cast gathering at 10 a.m. every Monday to read that week’s script. He sometimes stumbled over his dialogue or accidentally left out entire lines. Even a word like “invincible” could trip him up. His reading difficulties often interfered with his co-stars’ jokes. “I was constantly failing to give the right cue line, which would then screw up the joke for the person doing the scene with me,” said Winkler. Winkler asked to receive his scripts early so he could read them repeatedly before joining the rest of the cast. He knew this put extra pressure on the show’s writers. His castmates were supportive, but he often felt like he was letting them down. Winkler said, “All this at the height of my fame and success, as I was playing the coolest guy in the world.” The Fonz becomes a singing superstar. Photo Credit: ABC Television/ Wikimedia Commons A dyslexia diagnosis at age 31 He was already playing the Fonz when he began to understand why reading had always been so difficult for him. When his stepson was diagnosed with dyslexia, Winkler recognized many of the same problems he’d experienced growing up. His initial reaction to his own diagnosis was anger. He thought about the arguments with his parents and the punishments he’d received for getting poor grades. He finally understood that those difficulties weren’t the result of a lack of effort. Henry Winkler discusses his experiences with dyslexia at the Foreign Office in London in 2013. Photo Credit: Foreign and Commonwealth Office / Wikimedia Commons / OGL v1.0 From struggling to read books to writing them Winkler eventually added children’s author to his resume. Together with author Lin Oliver, he created the Hank Zipzer series, featuring a boy with dyslexia whose adventures are based on Winkler’s childhood. The books allowed Winkler to reach children experiencing some of the same frustrations he had growing up. Reading remains difficult for Winkler. He prefers to buy hardcover books and keeps the ones he’s read on his bookshelf. “Every one of them is a triumph,” Winkler told the Yale Center for Dyslexia & Creativity. The post The actor who played the Fonz couldn’t easily read the scripts. He found his own way through. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.titleOriginal: How this ‘harsh parenting rule’ helped save 99.8 percent of people during a historic tsunami

Μια αεροσυνοδός στέκεται συχνά στο διάδρομο και λέει κάποια παραλλαγή του: «Πάντα να φοράτε πρώτα τη δική σας μάσκα οξυγόνου πριν βοηθήσετε άλλους». Ακούμε αυτή τη φράση τόσο συχνά που πολλοί συντονίζονται. Αλλά είναι…
items.descriptionOriginal: Most of us, who have ever traveled on an airplane, are familiar with the notion of securing our safety before we secure the safety of those around us. A flight attendant often stands in the aisle and says some variation of: “Always put on your own oxygen mask first before assisting others.” We hear this sentence so often that many tune out. But its sentiment is essential: you can’t help others if you, yourself, are in peril. The concept in Japan is known as Tsunami-tendenko. As explained in a research paper by Susumu Cato and Ken Oshitani for National Library of Medicine , it’s a guide that applies to all. “‘Tsunami-tendenko,’ a guideline suggesting that individuals prioritize their own safety over aiding others during large-scale disasters.” Putting one’s self first The concept, according to Japanese newspaper The Mainichi isn’t known by everyone. “‘Tsunami tendenko,’ which come from the Tohoku dialect, means, ‘If a tsunami hits, each person should evacuate immediately on their own without caring about others, including their family.’ They further explain the origin. “The words were put together in 1990 by late tsunami researcher Fumio Yamashita, a native of Ofunato, Iwate Prefecture, who survived the 1933 Showa Great Sanriku Tsunami. After the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake, the word has come under the spotlight in tsunami evacuation measure promotions.” Hard for outsiders to understand In a post on X, Nobunaga ( @japan_nobunaga ) discusses the concept, sharing how the idea might be controversial for some. “For generations along Japan’s Sanriku coast, parents taught their children a tsunami rule that sounds almost cruel to outsiders: ‘Run for high ground alone. Do not come looking for Mom or Dad.’ Locals call it ‘Tsunami Tendenko,’ meaning each person must flee immediately on their own feet.” In the past, those who didn’t use the tactic might find themselves in irreversible danger. “In coastal history, entire families died together because brave mothers ran back toward schools while loyal children ran home looking for their parents, meeting the black wall of water halfway.” ‘Sacred family pact’ The concept was so important that some Japanese schools made it somewhat of a mantra. Nobunaga explains, “So Professor Toshitaka Katada and schools in Kamaishi City spent years turning that harsh old saying into a sacred family pact: ‘Mom promises she will run to survive, so trust her and run as high as you can without looking back.’” He shares a specific story. “At 2:46 p.m. on March 11, 2011, when the magnitude 9.0 earthquake shook the coast, teenagers at Kamaishi East Junior High didn’t wait for announcements. They bolted uphill in their indoor gym sneakers, shouting at everyone on the street to run, grabbing the cold hands of terrified elementary school kids from the neighboring building, and pushing wheelbarrows carrying exhausted toddlers even higher when the first designated shelter didn’t look safe enough.” Following this guideline saved nearly all of them. “Minutes later, waves over thirty feet high swallowed their classrooms whole. Out of 2,926 elementary and junior high school students across Kamaishi that afternoon, 2,921 survived, a 99.8 percent survival rate in a city that lost over a thousand residents.” Trusting the promise Luckily, for some moms, there was a happy ending. “When frantic mothers finally climbed the snowy hill hours later with soot on their coats, their children were waiting at the top alive because every single person trusted the promise.” View this post on Instagram Many on the X thread share they were taught the notion, as well. “My mother taught me that when I was a child in Hawaii. Run for the highest ground. Don’t wait, don’t look back.” Another agrees, “That is how you handle disaster. Have a working plan that makes everyone responsible for their own survival.” The post How this ‘harsh parenting rule’ helped save 99.8 percent of people during a historic tsunami appeared first on Upworthy .

Ένα άλλο είναι ότι οι γονείς αισθάνονται ότι δεν πήραν ποτέ το όνομα που πραγματικά ήθελαν να είναι…
items.descriptionOriginal: Baby name regret is surprisingly common amongst new mothers. A poll by Baby Center found that around 9% of mothers experience it after giving birth . There are many reasons why it happens; the big one is that they choose a name and after the baby arrives, it just doesn’t fit. Another is that parents feel they never got the name they truly wanted because they had to compromise with a partner. In some cases, parents may love a baby’s name but start having problems when others have trouble pronouncing or spelling it. Baby Center says that in 6% of cases, the moms have had the baby’s name changed legally. Nearly 1 in 10 moms regret the name they chose for their baby, according to survey https://t.co/iTvwkX6RjG — CBS News (@CBSNews) September 7, 2024 Many who keep the name they don’t like choose to give the baby a nickname, use their middle name, or refer to them by a shortened version of their birth name. Recently, a woman on Reddit shared a story that sparked debate: she loves her baby’s name, Genevieve Elise, but after 5 months wants to change it to Juliette because some people don’t know how to say or spell it. Why do people have a problem with Genevieve? “It didn’t even occur to me how many people would have trouble pronouncing/spelling/even getting used to the name. I mean it’s a pretty established name,” the mother wrote. “Nonetheless, I’ve decided to change it because while I absolutely adore the name, I don’t want to set her up for a lifetime of corrections and people either making fun or having a hard time with her name. I’ve been losing sleep over this!” Stressed young couple with baby. Credit: Canva What’s interesting is that Genevieve is a fairly common name. According to the Social Security Administration, it ranks 158th among the most popular female names from 2020 to 2025, right next to Reagan and Ember. The name has ancient French and Germanic roots, meaning “family wife,” “clan,” “kin,” and “lineage.” Its Welsh equivalent, Gwenhwÿfar, means “white spirit” or “white phantom”. The mother says she began to have problems shortly after the baby’s birth. “The comments/weird faces started early, surprisingly in the hospital!” the mother continued. “My pp nurse looked frustrated when I said it and said, ‘Alright, how do you spell that?’ Then the night shift nurse that same day said, ‘You moms and your creative names.’ I was so confused because I didn’t think an older name like this one would be considered creative!” Woman can’t sleep at night. Credit: Canva The commenters overwhelmingly disagreed with the name change Commenters overwhelmingly believed she should keep the name, noting that as it gains popularity, fewer people will have trouble speaking or spelling it. “Genevieve is one of the top 150 names in the USA! It’s growing in popularity and by the time she is 5, more people will be more familiar with it and know how to spell it,” one of the top commenters wrote. “5 months postpartum is a really difficult time emotionally and mentally for many women!” Ultimately, the commenters gave the mother some solid advice. The name regret may be caused by postpartum anxiety or depression, so it may be smart to wait a while before deciding. “I know this all sounds irrational; a few of you have pointed out PPA/PPD, which thank you so much for that!” the mom concluded. “Didn’t think this could be a sign, but totally makes sense. Might be wise to refrain from making any major changes right now. The post A woman loved her baby’s name, but after 5 months she wants to change it to Juliette appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: The phrase “age is just a number” is a popular idiom in American culture. When it comes to aging, it’s a cliché that rings true for many who refuse to let their chronological age define who they are. And Gen Xers are one generation that has really taken it to heart. Gen Xers, those born between 1965 and 1980, are currently 46-61 years old today. But they’re a generation that doesn’t feel that “old”. Many Gen Xers have reported feeling the magic number of 35 years old. And science backs them up, according to a study published in the journal Psychonomic Bulletin & Review , where researchers studied 1,470 Danish adult participants between the ages of 20 and 97. They found that of participants over the age of 40, an impressive 20% reported feeling younger than their chronological age. Translation: Gen Xers today may actually feel that they are 36-48 years old. Why Gen X feels younger than they are What set Gen Xers apart age-wise in the study was their acceptance of a “lifespan-developmental view”. This is defined as a psychological theory that people tend to choose an internal age that they consistently view themselves as, called an “attractor age”. For study participants, that was deemed to be 25 years old. This age serves as a “psychological anchor” of comparison, likely because at 25, true adulthood begins in terms of many significant aspects of life being established, including career, financial independence, romantic relationships, and the start of families. While decades may stack on to the age of 25, study participants noted it was still an age they could identify with—which influenced the concept of always feeling younger than they are. For example, of the study participants who were older than 39 years old, 70% reported that they actually felt younger than their chronological age. And after 40, participants reported feeling nearly 20% younger. Researchers noted that participants were not in denial about aging—but that they simply still felt psychologically connected to a time when they felt younger. More research on Gen Xers and aging A 2019 study also supports older generations feeling decades younger than they actually are. Researchers this time asked participants who were between the ages of 65 to 90 years old (technically making them Baby Boomers) how old they felt. Study participants also had additional health challenges due to aging—between two and six illnesses, ranging from cancer to arthritis to diabetes and more. Despite their health issues, the participants nonetheless reported that they felt an average of just 51 years old. “The social construction of age layers a multifaceted set of expectations for behavior and lifestyle,” researchers wrote. They found that perceived age came down to an individual’s “resilience” and “persistence”. “We suggest that the key factor is an abiding, resilient inner self, whose subject ‘age inside’ is not dependent on health or illness, family or situation, but on a particular point in the life course,” they added. “The persistence of a young age inside may reflect the desire to retain the higher status of youth or the identification with a younger self or the rejection of the stigma associated with old age.” The post Gen Xers keep saying they feel 35. A lifespan study puts that number in perspective. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Cold floors, chilly corners, and the familiar hunt for a sunny spot in the house are all part of winter. Growing up, many of us watched our grandparents prepare for the season by bringing out thick cotton razais , spreading handwoven durries , and opening curtains to let the afternoon sun in. These simple habits can still help us stay comfortable, reduce electricity bills, and make better use of things we already own. Here are eight traditional and sustainable ways to keep your home warmer this winter without constantly relying on a room heater. 1. Make the most of the winter sun Open curtains and shutters in rooms that receive direct sunlight during the day. Let sunlight fall on floors, walls, and furniture. Once evening approaches, draw the curtains to reduce the chill coming through windows. Cold floors, chilly corners, and the familiar hunt for a sunny spot in the house are all part of winter. Photograph: (Architectural Digest) Thicker curtains can provide an additional layer between the room and cold window panes. This is a humble form of passive solar heating. Traditional homes in our country were often designed around local climates, using natural light, ventilation, and locally available materials. Vernacular architecture in India offers useful examples of how traditional building designs work with natural conditions to create comfortable living spaces. 2. Bring out the traditional razais and quilts A well-filled cotton razai , woollen blanket, or quilt can make a bed comfortable without consuming electricity. Layer a lighter blanket beneath a thicker quilt on particularly cold nights. Keep an additional throw near the sofa for chilly evenings. Instead of replacing bedding every winter, air it on a dry, sunny day and repair loose seams or worn covers. Store it only when completely dry, preferably in a clean cotton bag. Reusing and maintaining bedding helps extend its life and reduces unnecessary purchases. 3. Cover cold floors with durries and rugs Stone and tiled floors can feel particularly cold during winter mornings. Place cotton durries, woollen rugs, or existing carpets in frequently used areas, such as beside the bed, near the sofa, and in a reading corner. Place cotton durries, woollen rugs, or existing carpets in frequently used areas. Photograph: (Amazon.in) You do not need to cover the entire floor. A few strategically placed rugs can make everyday spaces more comfortable. If you already own a handwoven durrie, bring it out instead of purchasing a new synthetic carpet. Shake it outdoors regularly and keep it dry to prevent dampness and unpleasant smells. 4. Layer clothing with natural fabrics A woollen sweater, shawl, socks, and comfortable slippers can make sitting in a chilly room considerably more pleasant. Wear a few layers that can be added or removed as temperatures change. Woollen garments and hand-me-downs can last for several years when cared for properly. If you need something new, consider repairing an old garment or buying a durable piece from a local maker instead of choosing something that may only last one season. 5. Use old fabric to block cold air Cold air can enter through gaps beneath doors and around windows. Instead of buying plastic draught stoppers, repurpose old household textiles. Roll an old towel or stitch leftover cotton fabric into a long cushion and place it beneath doors to limit cold air entering from outside. Check window frames for gaps and use suitable removable sealing strips where necessary. However, avoid blocking ventilation openings, particularly in kitchens and bathrooms, as homes need adequate airflow. 6. Spend more time in one sunny room Rather than trying to keep every room equally warm, arrange your daily activities in the part of the house that receives the most sunlight. If you already own a handwoven durrie, bring it out instead of purchasing a new synthetic carpet. Photograph: (Image generated by AI) Move a chair, work desk, or floor cushion closer to a sunny spot during the day. Close doors to rooms that are not being used, particularly those that remain noticeably colder. This helps you make better use of naturally available warmth without needing additional appliances. 7. Take inspiration from traditional Himalayan homes Traditional homes in colder parts of the country provide useful lessons in sustainable construction. In Himachal Pradesh, Kath-Kuni houses use alternating layers of stone and timber , with thick walls and mud plaster. Their construction helps insulate interiors and retain warmth. The revival of Kath-Kuni architecture in Himachal Pradesh shows how traditional building techniques and locally available materials can preserve architectural knowledge. Similarly, homes in Ladakh have traditionally used mud, stone, willow, and poplar to respond to the region's harsh winters. Traditional building techniques in Ladakh offer examples of how natural materials can be incorporated into contemporary homes. While these construction techniques cannot directly be replicated in apartments, they demonstrate the importance of choosing materials and designs suited to local climates. 8. Keep your home dry and ventilated Damp rooms can feel colder and may encourage mould growth. Dry wet clothes outdoors when the weather permits, wipe condensation from windows, and use kitchen and bathroom exhaust fans when cooking or bathing. A woollen sweater, shawl, socks, and comfortable slippers can make sitting in a chilly room considerably more pleasant. Photograph: (Pexels) Open windows briefly when outdoor conditions are suitable to allow fresh air to circulate. Keeping a home warm should not mean sealing it completely. Adequate ventilation is important for maintaining a healthy indoor environment. A warmer home through mindful choices Keeping your home comfortable during winter does not always require expensive appliances or renovations. Traditional architecture also offers lessons in building homes that respond to their surroundings. By combining these practices with mindful consumption, households can stay comfortable while reducing unnecessary energy use. These measures may not replace safe heating during severe cold , but they can reduce the need to rely on room heaters constantly.

items.descriptionOriginal: Welcome back to our weekly behind-the-scenes glimpse at what’s getting our team talking. Tell us what you’ve been reading at info@reasonstobecheerful.world and we just might feature it here. City of tomorrow At first glance, the sky seems to be the limit for Utah City, a new community in one of Utah’s fastest-growing cities, with the developer citing the cost of constructing high rises as the only constraint. The development checks all the boxes for the kind of sustainable, pedestrian-first urban living we often cover at RTBC: high density, walkability, green spaces, convenient transit options. And the project is ambitious , expected to be finished in 15 to 20 years. But Utah City faces heavy scrutiny, as Grist and the Salt Lake Tribune report in a story shared by Editorial Director Rebecca Worby. Though one new resident describes it as “rad” and “vibey,” members of the local city council call it a “gamble,” expressing skepticism that such a community makes sense in a place full of freeways and single-family homes. As one council member put it: “Walkability I don’t care about. [It] forces a lifestyle the average person isn’t living. Most people drive a car.” Becca says: If you build it, will they come? This is a fascinating look at a dense, transit-centered development that seems great on paper but may not be compatible with local desires. Popularity contest Imagine the U.S. without red states or blue states, just millions of people whose votes all matter equally. That’s what would happen if we got rid of the Electoral College, and according to a New York Times opinion piece shared by Executive Editor Will Doig, thanks to this month’s election, this idea is closer than ever to becoming a reality. Now that Arizona, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Nevada and Wisconsin will have Democratic governors and Democratic majorities in their legislatures, those states may sign the National Popular Vote Interstate Compact. As its name suggests, the compact would make it so that presidential elections are decided by the popular vote. Eighteen states have already adopted it, and if these five sign, writes Jesse Wegman, senior fellow at the Brennan Center for Justice, “then as early as November 2028 we could experience something no one has ever seen — a presidential election in which all Americans’ votes count equally and the candidate who gets the most votes wins.” Will says: I’d been half-listening to the news about states abandoning the Electoral College, but I hadn’t fully absorbed how profoundly this could impact American democracy — in a good way — until I read this piece . What else we’re reading Himalayan Communities Are Relying on Centuries-Old Water Solutions In the Face of Climate Change — shared by RTBC Founder David Byrne from Time Goats vs. vines: Baby goats devour invasive plants, save native trees in Mecklenburg County — shared by Will Doig from WFAE NYC Citi Bike member rides to be capped at $3.65 after Mamdani inks new deal with Lyft — shared by Rebecca Worby from Gothamist From our readers… Earlier this year, we published a story about wild European bison returning to the Carpathian Mountains of southwestern Romania. This week, we heard from Alex at Live Species , a small independent site that shows the latest published count for each of the world’s rarest wild animals, and those, like bison, whose numbers have recovered enough to tick up past 1,000. “The bison page shows none living free in 1927 and 9,762 in free-living herds in December 2024, a head count from the European Bison Pedigree Book,” writes Alex. “The page also credits WWF-Romania and Rewilding Europe for moving bison into the Țarcu Mountains, where they now range free.” Thanks, Alex! The post What We’re Reading: Building a Walkable City From Scratch appeared first on Reasons to be Cheerful .
